chains.title: application start -> libengine.so is loaded
chains.goal: Show how the sample reaches its protected native code at all: the name 'engine' never appears in the dex string pool, it is built byte by byte.

hops.text: Lcom/snake/App;-><clinit>()V invokes System.loadLibrary
the library name is built by fill-array-data, 6 payload bytes = 'engine'
the loader maps lib/arm64-v8a/libengine.so
the loader then calls the 44 .init_array constructors before JNI_OnLoad
and finally hands control to the exported JNI_OnLoad

chains.title: JNI_OnLoad: two RWX pages, a synthesised branch opcode, two jumps out
chains.goal: JNI_OnLoad registers nothing itself (0 JNIEnv slot loads in 12,280 bytes of Ghidra decompilation). What it does instead is build code: this is the hop sequence that explains why the registration sites live elsewhere.

hops.text: sysconf - page size for the coming mmap
svc #222 mmap(NULL, len, PROT_RWX, MAP_PRIVATE|ANON) - the first writable+exec page
br through a 4-entry relative-offset table
rand - entropy mixed into the synthesised opcode
the B opcode is written word by word into the fresh page
page n-1 is patched to branch to page n
FUN_0091ad58 (Ghidra) over the written range
blr into the generated page - control leaves the static image
second RWX mmap
blr into the second generated table; the return value selects the path
svc #53 fchmodat on a value taken from the generated page
strlen - the two length checks (11 and 10) that gate the byte-decode loops

chains.note: Both blr are accounted for (F4: blr_count = 2); the 4 svc are the only syscalls in the decoded 420 instructions.
chains.title_th: JNI_OnLoad: หน้า RWX 2 หน้า, opcode branch ที่สังเคราะห์เอง, และทางออก 2 ครั้ง
